text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today after climbing 15.6% over the past two weeks, likely a pullback following the announcement that the Trump administration will import Russian diesel to help ease fuel prices. That deal undercuts the refining margins U.S. refiners like Marathon have been enjoying—while crude oil at $96 per barrel and diesel in storage at just 105 million barrels had created a tight supply picture that boosted refiner profits, an influx of cheaper Russian diesel compresses those gains. The stock rose sharply yesterday on the geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Eastern Europe, which had been pushing oil and fuel prices higher, but today's retreat reflects reality: increased diesel supply from Russia directly threatens the high-margin environment refiners have been profiting from.

The broader context is that U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% utilization amid genuine supply constraints—hurricane damage in the Gulf, tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, and war disruptions have kept fuel tight and profitable for refiners. The Russian diesel agreement essentially trades that leverage away to achieve lower consumer prices, which is good for the economy but bad for refining company earnings.
